title: The commit-triggered workflows run the required check set on every branch-model-defined trigger event
asA: operator on an rcf-lite project with delivery-ci-workflows v2 applied
iWant: the commit-triggered workflows the materialiser produced (pull-request-checks and default-branch-checks per the elicited branch model) to run the required check set on every trigger event that branch model defines
soThat: no change reaches the default or trunk branch without the RCF chain, its coverage, and every enabled elicited check having been verified against the tree at the head commit

acceptanceCriteria.description: The CI provider's jobs for the commit-triggered workflows are triggered by the trigger events the branch model defines: for feature-branch, pushes to the default branch and pull requests opened, synchronised, or reopened against the default branch; for trunk-based, pushes to the trunk branch and (in the `trunkPullRequests: sometimes` sub-shape) pull requests targeting the trunk branch. The trigger configuration is committed under source control, not set through a provider UI.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the project's materialised workflow files and repository state at the head commit
acceptanceCriteria.when: a trigger event fires that the elicited branch model names
acceptanceCriteria.then: the aggregate pipeline report at the configured stable path (default `.rcf/reports/ci/pipeline.json`) is written by the resulting CI job, and its `trigger` field records the event kind and the workflow that ran

acceptanceCriteria.description: The merge policy blocks a merge whose most recent aggregate pipeline run did not exit zero. The block is enforced by the repository's branch protection or the equivalent platform policy per the branch-model AC binding (AC-6114-3 for feature-branch; AC-6115-1 or AC-6115-2 for trunk-based).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a change (a pull request in feature-branch or the with-PR trunk sub-shape, or a direct push in the trunk without-PR sub-shape) whose most recent aggregate pipeline run's report records `verdict: failed`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator or an automated merge tool attempts to admit the change through the standard merge or push path
acceptanceCriteria.then: the platform refuses the change, and the refusal reason references the failed required check that corresponds to the workflow that ran
